title: Flood Refund Need: Renewal-Date and Quarter-Block Counting of Premiums on File
content:
For a returned flood premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the insurance part of the flood refund need depends on how many flood insurance payments the reserve made within the twelve months before the handling date — flood payments on the reserve's ledger dated no later than the handling date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it.

**Exactly one flood payment — renewal dates.** The annual hazard premium on file counts in full only when the next hazard renewal, one year after the due date of the latest paid hazard insurance bill, is fewer whole months from the handling date than the horizon months; the annual flood premium on file counts in full only when the next flood renewal, one year after the due date of the latest paid flood insurance bill, is fewer whole months away than the horizon months. The premiums that count are added together; one with no paid bill of its kind adds nothing.

**Two or more flood payments — quarter blocks.** Each started quarter of the horizon carries a quarter of the annual hazard and flood premiums on file: the number of started quarters (horizon months divided by three, a fraction counting as a whole quarter) times one quarter of the two premiums together.

**No flood payment.** This rule does not apply.

The latest paid bill of a kind is the paid bill of that kind with the latest due date; months to a renewal are whole calendar months from the handling date to the renewal date, below zero where it has passed.

| Hypothetical case (hazard 1,200.00, flood 720.00 on file) | Insurance part |
|---|---|
| One flood payment; horizon 4; hazard renews in 7 whole months, flood in 3 | 720.00 |
| One flood payment; horizon 4; both renew in 1 whole month | 1,920.00 |
| Two flood payments; horizon 4 | 2 started quarters times 480.00: 960.00 |
